engagements.title: Employed, remote
engagements.body: Backend or full-stack on a product team. Most valuable where correctness and latency matter: pipelines, permissions, reporting, money.
points: Overlaps European mornings and US East Coast afternoons
Written-first: decision records, documentation, async updates

engagements.title: Architecture
engagements.body: Whave hired me to design a system, not build it. Schema, API surface, failure modes, written up so your team can execute.
points: Technical review of proposals and vendor quotes

engagements.title: Build and hand over
engagements.body: A defined system, built to a spec I help write, delivered with documentation and transferred to your team.
points: Discovery and written specification before any code
Database design, API, front end, deployment
Handover documentation and a walkthrough with your team

engagements.title: Systems for member organisations
engagements.body: Clubs, associations, districts and NGOs. Attendance, membership, dues, donations, reporting and awards. I've built for these problems repeatedly and understand them from the inside.
points: Reporting and exports that survive an audit

engagements.title: Rescue
engagements.body: Something exists and isn't working. I audit it, tell you honestly whether to fix or replace, then do it.
points: Build, fix or replace recommendation with reasoning
Migration plan if you decide to move

process.title: Conversation
process.body: Thirty minutes. What you're trying to do, what's in the way, and whether I'm the right person. Sometimes I'm not, and I'll say so.

process.title: Written scope
process.body: Before anything is built: what's included, what isn't, what it costs and when it lands. If we disagree, we disagree on paper, cheaply.

process.title: Build in the open
process.body: Regular demos of working software, not status reports. You see it as it becomes real and can change your mind while changing it is cheap.

process.title: Handover
process.body: Documentation, credentials, a walkthrough, and a support window. The goal is that you don't need me afterwards.
